key_insight: A 145,281-parameter multi-head quantum neural network replaced eight contiguous transformer blocks in a 30-billion-parameter LLM, displacing 16.33% of its parameters with limited accuracy loss.
engineering_relevance: Partitioning hidden states into small quantum heads enables NISQ-compatible modules to integrate into production-scale LLMs without encoding the full hidden width at once.
method: Partition 2,048 hidden dimensions into 32 heads, each angle-encoded into an 8-qubit register.
Process heads with four-layer quantum circuits and learned readouts, coupled through constrained classical linear mixers.
Train using exact statevector simulation, then execute quantum heads on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 included held-out perplexity ablations: mixers alone came within 1–3% of the full module for fused spans, while a parameter-matched classical MLP performed a few percent better.
watch_item: Quantum-specific advantage remains unproven: limited-seed controls with disabled entanglers or frozen circuits beat the full module on held-out perplexity.
paper_title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
